Thank you so much for Appwrite! The community on Discord is very helpful and the self hosting guide is great. Very unlike my terrible experience with Supabase who seem to do their best to cripple the self hosted option

Appwrite is written in PHP... AppWrite doesn't yet have their Cloud version, so they aren't ready to be a 'backend as a service'... it seems like the project doesn't move as fast as its competitor (primarily Supabase) for features I care about, and perhaps this is caused by PHP?

I've been looking into supabase for a long time... after many months of keeping an eye on them, appwrite comes along and i'm instantly sold... Supabase is just fancy ui and marketing, while these guys seem the real deal.

Strictly speaking, if I spin up a droplet on DO and install Appwrite on it, it won't be a BAAS anymore, correct? Sorry but "self-host your own BAAS" is an oxymoron. IMO, developers who chose Firebase do not want to manage servers.

Appwrite is more about simplicity. Our SDKs are simple, our UI is simple, our Documentation is simple, heck we even have a 1 line deploy... Use a part of Appwrite, or all of it... we just want you to do more while writing less code.

Looks real slick!... it's nice to have something easy to integrate with for common stuff like user management etc., but the offline dev story there is lacking. Nice to see Appwrite provides a containerized solution for that, should make distributed dev (and testing!) a lot easier.
What are the backends for storage and database and how easy would it be to change or scale? A quick search didn't lead to any architecture information or tech stack details.
Appwrite is my backend of choice since I learned it. Stable release is AMAZING news for me!
This is the most overly positive and least critical HN submission I've ever seen

@dang and HN mods - please help cull the bot / employee / astroturf comments dominating the comments here... the comment spam footgun makes me sad, bc the stuff you're building actually looks worthwhile.

It's a tough segment to build a business in. It's crowded, and these kinds of opinionated abstractions are limiting once you want flexibility or scale. Still, people are looking for good open source options... Someone has to keep Supabase honest...
